posts.title: MG 07 gets over 10,000 firm orders in under 2 minutes as MG ramps up capacity
posts.summary:
The MG 07 surpassed 10,000 firm orders in 1 minute and 57 seconds, far faster than the MG4's previous record of 39 minutes and 37 seconds.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The MG 07 achieved 10,000 firm orders in just 1 minute and 57 seconds, significantly outpacing the MG4's previous record of nearly 40 minutes.
Total pre-orders reached 59,000 by the day after launch, with firm orders indicating high conversion intent compared to refundable reservations.
MG has aggressively scaled its retail footprint, increasing sales outlets and pop-up locations to approximately 600, a threefold increase from the previous year.
Consumer demand for long-range variants exceeded forecasts, with models offering over 800 kilometers of range accounting for more than 45% of orders.
To mitigate potential supply bottlenecks, MG proactively collaborated with CATL to add two dedicated battery production lines following strong initial pre-order data.

posts.title: Geely Auto core profit jumps 46% in H1 as home market retreats
posts.summary:
Geely Auto's first-half revenue rose 15% year-on-year to a record 173.6 billion yuan ($25.58 billion), while core profit increased 46%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Auto reported a 46% increase in core net profit to 9.68 billion yuan for the first half of 2026, despite a 2% decline in reported net profit due to foreign-exchange fluctuations.
The company's shift toward higher-priced models, such as the Zeekr 9X, successfully raised the average selling price per vehicle by 15,000 yuan.
While revenue reached a record 173.6 billion yuan, the company continues to face domestic headwinds, with local sales falling 22.6% while overseas exports surged 158%.

posts.title: Geely Auto reshuffles top management to advance One Geely strategy
posts.summary:
Geely Auto is undergoing its biggest senior management reshuffle since founding, with Eric Li stepping down as chairman and Andy An taking over.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Auto founder Eric Li is stepping down as chairman, transitioning to the role of honorary chairman for life while remaining chairman of the parent Geely Holding Group.
Andy An, current CEO of Geely Holding, will succeed Li as chairman of Geely Auto to lead the implementation of the 'One Geely' strategy.
The reshuffle represents a major corporate governance shift toward professional management, moving the company away from its founder-driven startup roots.

posts.title: CATL says core operations carbon neutral by end-2025, supply chain next
posts.summary:
CATL said its supply chain accounts for more than 80% of its products' carbon emissions, and it aims to achieve value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: CATL has achieved carbon neutrality across its core manufacturing operations as of the end of 2025, utilizing 100% zero-carbon electricity across its production facilities.
The company has set a new target to reach full value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035, a critical step as supply chain activities account for over 80% of its total product lifecycle emissions.
Despite scaling production to 748 GWh in 2025, CATL reduced its carbon-emissions intensity by approximately 77% over the last two years through energy efficiency improvements.
To manage its supply chain transition, CATL is leveraging its proprietary Carbon Chain Management System to track real-world carbon data from mineral extraction through component manufacturing.

posts.title: What Flock’s defenders are missing
posts.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Flock, the police-tech giant known for its network of some 120,000 automatic license plate readers around the US, announced some changes to its platform last Thursday. The updates are meant to prevent…
bullets: Flock operates a massive network of approximately 120,000 automatic license plate readers across the US, positioning it as a dominant player in the police-tech sector.
The company is implementing new safeguards, such as abnormal search flagging and mandatory case number entry, following reports of officers using the system for stalking and harassment.
Critics argue these technical controls are easily bypassed by entering fraudulent data, failing to address fundamental concerns regarding the platform's evolution into a mass surveillance network.
Growing public and legal backlash has led some municipalities to cancel contracts, creating significant regulatory and reputational risk for the company's long-term business model.
